newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Pakhoed confident about years ahead.
newsitem.headline: Pakhoed confident about years ahead.

text.p: Dutch tank storage and shipping group Pakhoed NV said on Tuesday it was positive about profit developments in coming years.

"As chemical manufacturers are concentrating on their core business of manufacturing and marketing, Pakhoed is confident it can capture opportunities to fulfil a key role in logistics and distribution," the company said.

Even after deduction of a 12 million guilder dividend to holders of preference shares, the 1997 net profit is expected to be substantially higher than 1996's 138.3 million net from ordinary operations, Pakhoed said.
Chemical distribution will fully contribute to the current year's results with the turn-around of the U.S. operations in full swing.
The oil-storage activities in Rotterdam were expected to yield positive operating results because of the restructuring which took place in 1996.
Results of the shipping division were expected to show further growth, the company added.
Earlier, Pakhoed posted a 1996 net profit from ordinary operations of 138.3 million guilders, up from 123.6 million in the previous year and at the higher end of analysts' expectations.
Restructuring charges, which were mainly taken in the first half of the year, cut the 1996 total net profit to 75.5 million guilders from 1995's 121.5 million.
The charges were taken for the reorganisation of Pakhoed's Rotterdam-based units and the sale of troubled subsidiary Furness, which combines port activities, car dealerships and logistics.
Pakhoed also took over U.S. chemicals distributor Univar in 1996. The company said it was now market leader in the U.S. in the distribution business and second largest in Europe.
